segments.heading: Module comment: what `render` returns
segments.text: `build_facts.py` calls `render(D)` and gets two results: the verdict object and the text of FACTS.md [Ref1]. The comment says that the fixed texts of this file (the templates) hold words only, and that every number is formatted from the data that `build_facts.py` collected. It also says that each sentence that states a pattern of the data has a guard, a call of `need` (line 36). The script stops when the data do not show that pattern.

Imports.
- `statistics` gives the median. `Decimal` and `ROUND_HALF_UP` give the decimal rounding of `_q` (line 41).
- `facts_data`, short name `fd`, is the module with the parsers and the range functions [Ref2].
- `R`, `S`: the results folder and the folder of this script.
- `sel(records, field=value, ...)` returns the records that match every condition. A condition value may be one value, a set of allowed values, or a function.
- `rng(records)` returns a range: the lowest, the highest and the median `GBps`, and the counts of intervals, processes, sessions and boots.
- `overlap`, `gap`, `width_pct`: the three range functions that `compare` uses (line 333). `rel` shortens a path to `R/...` or `S/...`.

segments.heading: Constants: lists of earlier data sets
segments.text:
`W15` and `K13` are two folder paths from facts_data.py: the scratch folders of 2026-11-15 and of 2026-11-13. The three lists name earlier data sets, grouped by the runner program:
- `BW12`: `L-1` to `L-4`, runs of bwx12. `L-1` is the baseline, and the other three are supporting rows.
- `BW11`: `R0` and `R0b`, runs of the older runner bwx11.
- `BWX`: `B7a`, `B7b`, `C3a`, `C3b`, runs of the first runner bwx.

segments.heading: Constants: fixed texts
segments.text:
Fixed result texts.
- `DIFFERS`, `SAME`: the two wordings that `compare` (line 333) can give.
- `NO_READ`: the text for a comparison that the data cannot give. It says that no 8000 MT/s run of the kernel `read` with bwx12 exists.
- `ADDED`, `NOT_PLAN`: two labels. In this file both are attached to control I.

- `H1_MEAS`: the sentence that names the measurement which would resolve hypothesis H1 of section 6.
- `FIRST`: the value of the field `kernel_before` of the first interval of a bwx process. `render` selects with it (line 408). `build_facts.py` writes the same text into the records as its own literal [Ref1].
- `STANDIN`: a text for the row labels of part L. It says that asmread is used in place of the new read kernel. The comment above it quotes rule V4.
- `F2_NOTE`: a note on the rules that the comparison of part C with 8000 MT/s follows. This file does not use it. facts_text4.py imports it [Ref3].

segments.heading: Function `need`: the guard
segments.text: When `cond` is false, `need` raises `SystemExit` with a message that ends with the text `what`. Then `render` does not return. `build_facts.py` writes facts.json and FACTS.md only after `render` has returned [Ref1]. So a failed guard leaves both files as they were.

segments.heading: Function `_q`: decimal rounding, half up
segments.text:
`_q(x, step)` rounds `x` to the number of decimals of `step` and returns the result as text. This file calls it with the steps `'0.01'` and `'0.1'`.
- `round(x, 6)` rounds to 6 decimals, and `repr` gives the shortest decimal text of that number. This removes the small errors of binary floating-point numbers, for example 0.19999999999999998 in place of 0.2.
- `Decimal(...)` reads the text as an exact decimal number.
- `quantize` rounds it to the decimals of the step. A value exactly in the middle between two steps goes to the step that is farther from 0. For a positive value that is the higher step.
- Example: `_q(0.125, '0.01')` returns `0.13`. The Python format `%.2f` returns `0.12` for the same value.

segments.heading: Functions `g`, `sp`, `pc`: rates, ranges, percent values as text
segments.text:
- `g(x)`: a rate as text with 2 decimals (step 0.01 GB/s).
- `sp(a)`: a range as the text `lo to hi`. Both ends go through `g`.
- `pc(x)`: a percent value as text with 1 decimal (step 0.1).
- These functions only make the printed text. The statistics of `analyse` and `compare` use the values before rounding.

segments.heading: Function `pcr`: lowest and highest percent value
segments.text: `pcr(ds)` takes a list of percent values, for example the drops of all pairs of one part. It formats the lowest and the highest value with `pc`. When both texts are equal, it returns one value, for example `35.4 %` for the 2 drops of F72d12. Otherwise it returns both, for example `30.5 % to 31.2 %` for the 4 drops of the part C group `read after oldread` [Ref4].

segments.heading: Function `hm`: time of day
segments.text: Formats a time as `HH:MM:SS`.

segments.heading: Function `hmd`: time with its date
segments.text:
- `RERUN_DAY`: the day of the rerun. In the sheet, a time without a date is on this day.
- `hmd(t)` returns date and time as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`. When the date is not `RERUN_DAY`, it also adds the time of day to the set `OTHER_DAY`.
- `OTHER_DAY` is a global variable of the module. `render` empties it at its start (line 357), and `check_dates` reads it.

segments.heading: Function `check_dates`: find a time without its date
segments.text: It cuts every line of the finished sheet text into pieces. A piece ends at the end of a sentence (a period followed by white space) or at a table cell border (a `|` with one white-space character on each side). The function returns each piece that holds a time of day from `OTHER_DAY` and no date of the form `2026-MM-DD`. `render` calls it on the finished text (line 1486), and a guard stops the script when a piece is returned.

segments.heading: Function `dur`: seconds as text
segments.text: Rounds a number of seconds to whole seconds and formats it. Examples: `5 s`, `1 min 5 s`, `1 h 2 min 5 s`.

segments.heading: Function `nn`: the counts of a range as text
segments.text: `a` is a range (a result of `rng`). The result has the form `11 intervals / 7 processes / 1 boot`. With `sessions=True` the number of sessions is added before the boots. With `boots=False` the number of boots is left out.

segments.heading: Function `sess`: the sessions of a record list as text
segments.text:
- `rr`: only the records whose data set name starts with `rerun-`. The records of control I and of F72d12 are left out. So a list of such records gets the text `no session`.
- `ss`: the session numbers of `rr`, sorted, each once.
- `extra`: the number of processes in `rr` that have no session number. In the rerun that is T72C4, the fourth process of part C [Ref2].
- Three or more session numbers with no missing number between them give a count, for example `3 sessions`. Otherwise the numbers are listed, for example `sessions 1 and 3`.
- When `extra` is above 0, a text such as ` and 1 extra process` is added.

segments.heading: Function `nns`: full count text of rerun records
segments.text: Builds the text for n from a record list: intervals / processes / the text of `sess` / boots. The counts come from `rng(rs)`. Example: the 6 oldread records of part L give `6 intervals / 3 processes / 3 sessions / 1 boot` [Ref4].

segments.heading: Function `table`: the lines of one Markdown table
segments.text: Returns the lines of one table in Markdown, the plain-text format of FACTS.md. The lines are: the header line, the separator line, one line per row, and one empty line. The cells of a line stand between `|` characters.

segments.heading: Class `Refs`: the numbered file list of section 7
segments.text:
- `d` maps a key to a list of two items: the reference number and the description.
- `add(path, desc)`: the key is the absolute path. A name that starts with `ext:` marks an external source, and it is kept unchanged. A new key gets the next number, counted from 1. A key that is already in `d` is not changed.
- `__call__`: the call `ref(path)` returns the text `[RefN]` of a registered path. A path that was not registered raises `KeyError`.

segments.heading: Function `register`: number every file that the sheet cites
segments.text:
- `ref`: a new, empty object of the class `Refs`.
- `a`: a short name for `ref.add`. Each call `a(path, description)` below registers one file.
- A file gets its number at its first `a` call. So the order of the calls fixes the numbers `[RefN]` in the facts sheet.
- The rows below only name the files of each block.

Eight entries.
- The four scripts that build the sheet.
- The two existing statistics tools `stat_k120.py` and `stat_bwx.py`, used as a cross-check.
- The rules file.
- The record of the review that produced the rules.

The scripts and inputs of the run: `go.sh`, `ra.sh`, `go2.sh`, the three spec files, and the two sha256 files `local.sha` and `go2.sha`, which were written at launch. Then two copies of 8000 MT/s part A files with converted header lines. Their descriptions say that they are used only for the cross-check with `stat_k120.py`.

Files in the folders of the earlier work, and the two logs.
- `rx.sh`, `r0.sh` and `FINDINGS.md` in the folder `W15`. The rerun also used `rx.sh`. It is the runner script of parts L and C and of control I.
- `run_kernels.sh` in the folder `K13`.
- The log of go.sh and the log of go2.sh.
- Two descriptions quote the number of an integrity check (a check of the raw files and the scripts that `build_facts.py` ran). The code finds that number as the index of the check key (`sha-rx`, `A-args`) in the list `D['checks']`, plus 1. Python counts an index from 0.

The raw files of the rerun.
- For each of the 3 part A folders: `threads120.csv` and `probe.txt`.
- For each of the 9 bwx12 folders (3 of part L, 4 of part C, 2 of control I): the csv file, `env.txt`, `launches.txt` and `stderr.txt`.

The 8000 MT/s files of part A. For the data set `A-1`: `threads120.csv` of the test of 2026-11-13, its `probe.txt` and the csv of its one-thread part. For `A-2` and `A-3`: the files `A1.csv` and `A3.csv`, and the `env.txt` of their folder.

The files of the earlier bwx runs.
- For each data set in `D['rx']` (runs that `rx.sh` or `r0.sh` started): the csv file of each process that `build_facts.py` read, `env.txt`, `launches.txt` and `stderr.txt`. A folder can hold more csv files, and these get no entry. When `env.txt` holds no sha256 line of the binary, the description says that the sha256 is in `r0.sh`.
- For each data set in `D['step']` (runs of the first runner bwx): the csv file and `env.txt`. When several data sets use the same csv file, `same` lists them, and the description names all of them.

Records of the machine state.
- `try6.txt`, the file with the Linux kernel log times of the boots, and the boot list of the journal.
- The DIMM report.
- The saved journal and the saved Linux kernel log of the boot of 2026-11-09.
- A firmware settings list. Its description quotes the file time.
- Two external sources, named with `ext:`: a text of the Linux kernel documentation and the manual page proc(5).

Files and sources that were added with the corrections of the review. The comment says that they are numbered after the earlier entries.
- The second csv of the run folder of `A-2`.
- Four files of a save of Linux settings in the boot of 2026-11-09.
- The manual page ps(1), as an external source.

Files that were added with the corrections of verification round 3.
- Four files of the run folder that ended 8 s before the first process of `A-2`.
- The saved journal and the saved Linux kernel log of a 10-module boot.
- The module list of the boot of the rerun.
- The replies and the lists of the firmware settings tool, and the last reading of the memory speed setting.
- The function returns `ref`.

segments.heading: Function `med`: median rate of a record list
segments.text: Returns the median of the field `GBps` of the records in `rs`. `GBps` is the rate of one timed interval in GB/s. It is already in the record when this file runs [Ref1]. For 3 records the median is the middle value.

segments.heading: Function `analyse`: the pairs for Q1 and the selector `pool`
segments.text: `recs` is the list of all interval records, and `N` collects the results. `one(rs)` is a helper: a guard checks that the list `rs` holds exactly one record, and the helper returns that record. It is written as a tuple of two items (a fixed list in round brackets): the guard and the record. Python runs the guard first and returns the second item.

segments.heading: Part A: one pair per session and round
segments.text: The two loops give 6 pairs: one per session (1, 2, 3) and round (1, 2) of part A. `cell(b, k)` selects the records of the data set `rerun-A` with this session, this round, the binary `b` and the kernel `k`, and it sorts them by the interval number. In part A each binary runs each kernel in one process per round [Ref6]. So one `cell` holds the intervals of one process.

Four selections per pair:
- `old`: kernel `read` of `bw_old`, the old read kernel.
- `new`: kernel `read` of `bw_new`, the new read kernel.
- `ao`, `an`: kernel `asmread` of `bw_old` and of `bw_new`.
- The guard stops the script unless each selection holds exactly 3 records, the 3 timed intervals of one process.
- Part A also holds records of the kernels write, copy, asmwrite and asmcopy [Ref6]. No selection takes them, so they enter no pair.

`vo` and `vn` are the 3 rates of the old process and the 3 rates of the new process, in GB/s.
- Each rate is the field `GBps` of one record. For part A that is the value of column 7 (`aggregate_GBps`) of one interval row of `threads120.csv`, as the benchmark printed it with 2 decimals [Ref7].
- The line of the csv that starts with `# bandwidth:` gives the formula of the benchmark: the sum of the bytes of all threads, divided by the longest elapsed time of a thread [Ref7].
- The row `best` of a process holds the highest of its 3 interval rates [Ref7]. It is not an interval row. facts_data.py skips it, so no record holds it [Ref2].
- All 3 intervals are used, and no rates are added.

One dictionary per pair goes into `pa`, and `N['pa']` holds the 6 pairs.
- `old_med`, `new_med`: the median of the 3 old rates and of the 3 new rates. These are the two rates that the pair compares.
- `ratio` = `new_med / old_med`.
- `drop` = `(1 - new_med / old_med) * 100`, in percent.
- `ratio_lo` = lowest new rate / highest old rate. `ratio_hi` = highest new rate / lowest old rate.
- `ao_ratio`, `an_ratio`: the median of `bw_old asmread` and the median of `bw_new asmread`, each divided by `old_med`.
- Example, session 1, round 1: the old rates 467.83, 467.92 and 465.38 GB/s give `old_med` = 467.83 GB/s. The new rates 330.59, 330.09 and 333.25 GB/s give `new_med` = 330.59 GB/s. The drop is 29.34 % [Ref6].

segments.heading: Function `pairs`: old-against-new pairs of a bwx data set
segments.text: `pairs(dataset, kernels)` builds the pairs of one data set of a bwx runner. `tags` holds the tags of the data set, each once, in the order of their first record. In the five data sets used below one tag is one process, for example `T72L1` [Ref6].

For each process and for the rounds 0 and 1:
- `o`: the one `oldread` record of this process and round. The helper `one` stops the script when it finds no record or more than one.
- `r`: for each kernel `k` of the list, the one record of that kernel in the same process and round.
- `drop_<k>` = `(1 - r['GBps'] / o['GBps']) * 100`, in percent. Both rates are single intervals. No median is taken.
- `GBps` of a bwx record is a sum over the T rows of the interval (one row per thread): each thread gives `bytes / elapsed_s / 1e9`, and the values of all threads are added. `bytes` is column 7 and `elapsed_s` is column 8 of a T row [Ref8]. The column `aggregate_GBps` of the I row is not used for it [Ref1] [Ref2].
- The rounds are fixed to 0 and 1. A record of a later round would enter no pair. The five data sets below hold only the rounds 0 and 1 [Ref6].

Five calls. The pair counts are those of the data [Ref6].
- `N['pl']`: part L, asmread against oldread. 3 processes x 2 rounds = 6 pairs.
- `N['pi']`: control I, asmread against oldread. 2 processes x 2 rounds = 4 pairs.
- `N['pf']`: the earlier run F72d12, asmread against oldread. 1 process x 2 rounds = 2 pairs.
- `N['pc']`: part C, `read` and asmread against oldread. 4 processes x 2 rounds = 8 pairs, each with `drop_read` and `drop_asmread`.
- `N['p80']`: the 8000 MT/s baseline `L-1`, asmread against oldread, 2 pairs. No other line of facts_text.py or facts_text4.py reads it.
- The records of read_nop96, read_nop256 and read_1pl enter no pair.

segments.heading: Function `pool`: records of several data sets
segments.text: `pool(names, kernel, pos)` returns the records whose data set is one of `names` and whose kernel is `kernel`. When `pos` is given, the record must also have this position in the kernel sequence. `render` uses it to take the intervals of several 8000 MT/s data sets as one list (line 417). `analyse` stores the function as `N['pool']` and returns `N`.

segments.heading: Function `compare`: 7200 MT/s range against 8000 MT/s range
segments.text:
Takes two record lists and returns one comparison.
- `a`, `b`: the ranges of the 7200 MT/s list and of the 8000 MT/s list. Each range runs from the lowest to the highest `GBps` of its list. No interval is removed.
- `overlap`: true when `a.lo <= b.hi` and `b.lo <= a.hi` [Ref2]. Two ranges that share only one end value count as overlapping.
- `dist`: the distance of the nearest ends in GB/s. It is positive when `a` lies above `b`, negative when `a` lies below `b`, and 0 when they overlap.
- `wording`: `SAME` when the ranges overlap, `DIFFERS` when they do not.
- `width`: `(b.hi - b.lo) / b.lo * 100`, the width of the 8000 MT/s range in percent.

segments.heading: Function `render`: statistics, verdicts and the whole text
segments.text: The main function of the file, from line 341 to line 1488. It first calls `analyse` (the pairs) and `register` (the file list). `V` is the verdict object. Its entries start empty, except `rule_wordings`, which holds the three fixed texts `DIFFERS`, `SAME` and `NO_READ`.

Short names for parts of `D`, and the output list.
- `try6`: the boot record. `go`, `go2`: the logs of go.sh and go2.sh.
- `A`: the part A folders. `X`: the bwx12 folders.
- `ev`: the steps of the run. `evd`: the same steps by their folder tag. `p13`: the entry `probe13`. `rules`: the path of the rules file.
- `L` is the list of the text lines of FACTS.md. `w(text)` adds one line.
- `extra` collects short texts and values for `section4` of facts_text4.py. The comment names sections 1 to 3 as their source. The code sets both entries in section 1.5 (lines 1017 and 1128).
- `OTHER_DAY.clear()` empties the set that `hmd` fills.

segments.heading: Function `q2row`: one comparison row for facts.json
segments.text:
Appends one dictionary to `V['q2_rows']`. `c` is a result of `compare`.
- The row holds both ranges as they are (`lo_7200`, `hi_7200`, `lo_8000`, `hi_8000`), and the counts of intervals and processes of both sides.
- `distance_GBps` is `dist` rounded to 3 decimals (0.001 GB/s).
- `wording` is stored only when `decides` is true. Otherwise the field is `None`.
- `row_7200` and `scope_8000` are the keys of the row. The two `_label` fields hold the texts that FACTS.md prints. They default to the keys.
- This file does not call `q2row`. In line 1464 it passes the function to `section4` of facts_text4.py [Ref3].

segments.heading: Values that several sections use
segments.text:
- `go_start`, `go_end`: the times of the first and of the last state line in the log of go.sh. `go2_start`, `go2_end`: the same for go2.sh.
- `one_len(ds)`: a guard checks that all records of the data set `ds` have one value of `min_ms`, the minimum length of a timed interval in ms. The helper returns that length in seconds as text.
- `secA` is this minimum length for part A (`0.5 s`), and `secX` is the one for part L (`6 s`). A guard checks that part C and control I have the same value as part L. For part A, `build_facts.py` sets `min_ms` to the constant 500 [Ref1].
- `mib`: the buffer size of one thread as text, `256 MiB` (1 MiB = 2^20 bytes). It is the value of the column `kB_total` of the P rows, divided by 1024. A guard checks that all P rows of the 9 bwx12 files hold one value [Ref1].
- `f72t`: the launch time of the F72d12 process.

Guards on the time order of the rules file and the run.
- `rules_time`: the time in the line `# Written ...Z` of the rules file.
- `rules_lead`: the start of go.sh minus `rules_time`, in seconds. A guard needs a value above 0. So the time that the rules file states is earlier than the first state line of go.sh.
- `mtime(p)`: the time of the last change of the file `p`, in UTC, in whole seconds. The comment says that file times are on the clock of the agent's server, and that the start of go.sh is on the clock of CRB.
- Three more guards. The file time of the rules file equals `rules_time`. Line 2 of the rules file holds the words `BEFORE the run (go.sh not yet started)`. The file `local.sha` is newer than the rules file.

segments.heading: The drops of all pairs, and two guards for Q1
segments.text:
Six lists of drops in percent, one value per pair.
- `dl`, `di`, `df`: asmread against oldread in part L (6 values), in control I (4) and in F72d12 (2).
- `dcr`, `dca`: `read` against oldread and asmread against oldread in part C (8 values each).
- `dpa`: the drops of the 6 part A pairs.
- First guard: the lowest of all 34 drops is above 0. So the new side is below the old read kernel in every pair.
- Second guard: `ratio_hi` is below 1 in every part A pair. So the highest `bw_new read` interval is below the lowest `bw_old read` interval of the same pair.

segments.heading: Part C: groups by the kernel that ran directly before
segments.text:
`Crec` holds all records of part C. `cgroup(kernel, before)` builds one group.
- `rs`: the part C records of this kernel whose field `kernel_before` equals `before`.
- `ds`: for each record of `rs`, the drop of the pair in `N['pc']` that holds this same record. So each drop still compares the interval with the oldread interval of its own process and round.
- The guard needs as many drops as records, and at least one record.
- The function returns the two lists `rs` and `ds`.
- facts_data.py sets `kernel_before` from the kernel sequence in the header line of the csv, not from time stamps [Ref2].

The five groups, with the number of intervals in the rerun [Ref6]:
- `read after oldread`: 4 intervals, from the cfwd processes T72C1 and T72C3.
- `read after asmread`: 4 intervals, from the crev processes T72C2 and T72C4.
- `asmread after read`: 4 intervals (cfwd).
- `asmread first`: 2 intervals. asmread is the first interval of a crev process (round 0).
- `asmread after oldread`: 2 intervals. In round 1 of a crev process asmread follows oldread, the last kernel of round 0.
- The guard checks that the five groups together hold as many records as part C has `read` and asmread records. `N['CG']` stores the groups.

segments.heading: Record lists for Q2
segments.text:
Each list is made with `sel` or `pool`. The counts are those of the data [Ref6].
- `L72o`, `L72a`: oldread and asmread of part L (6 intervals each). `I72o`, `I72a`: control I (4 each). `F72o`, `F72a`: F72d12 (2 each).
- `P12o`: the 8000 MT/s pool of oldread at position 0 in the data sets `L-1` to `L-4` (11 intervals of 7 processes). `P12a`: asmread at position 1 in the same data sets (11 intervals). Each pool holds intervals of two lengths: 6 s in `L-1` (2 of the 11, the length of part L) and 4 s in `L-2` to `L-4` (9 of the 11) [Ref6].
- `PALLo`, `PALLa`: the same pools plus the bwx11 data sets `R0` and `R0b` (18 intervals each). This file does not use them itself. In lines 1461 and 1462 it passes them to facts_text4.py.
- `A72o`: `bw_old read` of part A, all sessions and rounds (18 intervals of 6 processes).
- `A80o`: `bw_old read` of the 8000 MT/s data sets `A-1`, `A-2` and `A-3` (21 intervals of 7 processes).
- `C72o`: oldread of part C at both of its positions, 0 in cfwd and 2 in crev (8 intervals of 4 processes).

Eight calls of `compare` (line 333). Each call takes all intervals of a list as one range from the lowest to the highest rate. No call here uses a record of the new read kernel.
- `cLo`, `cLa`: oldread and asmread of part L against `P12o` and `P12a`.
- `cIo`, `cIa`: control I against the same two pools.
- `cFo`, `cFa`: F72d12 against the same two pools.
- `cAo`: `bw_old read` of part A against `A80o`.
- `cCo`: oldread of part C against `P12o`.
- Example `cLo`: 461.61 to 464.29 GB/s against 465.53 to 470.05 GB/s. The ranges do not overlap, `dist` is -1.24 GB/s, and the wording is `DIFFERS` [Ref4] [Ref6].

segments.heading: Part A, session 1: load-only kernels against 8000 MT/s
segments.text:
The list `pa3` gets 6 entries: 3 kernels (`bw_new read`, `bw_new asmread`, `bw_old asmread`) x 2 rounds. The comment names rule V3.
- `s1`: the 3 intervals of session 1 of the rerun for this binary, kernel and round.
- `a1`, `a2`: the intervals of the 8000 MT/s data sets `A-1` and `A-2` for the same binary, kernel and round. `b80` is the range of both lists together.
- `above`: for each interval of `s1` above `b80.hi`, its distance to `b80.hi` in GB/s. `below`: the same for an interval below `b80.lo`.
- `inside` = 3 - the number above - the number below.
- `A-2` holds no `bw_old asmread` record. So for that kernel `b80` comes from the 3 intervals of `A-1` alone [Ref6].
- `newread`: the 2 entries of `bw_new read`.

segments.heading: Title and notes of FACTS.md
segments.text: Writes the title line and the list of notes under it: the source of the numbers, the units (GB = 1e9 bytes, times in UTC), the date rule, the folders `R` and `S`, the meaning of `[RefN]`, and the rounding. The rounding note says that rates are shown to 0.01 GB/s, half up, and that a difference of two rates is computed before rounding. So a printed difference can differ by 0.01 GB/s from the difference of the two printed rates. The last note says that fixed properties of the setup are written as the task and the run scripts give them: the CPU numbers of the two meshes, the loads per 256 B of each kernel, the two memory speeds, and the dates of earlier runs.

segments.heading: Section 0: heading and guards of the Short version
segments.text:
Writes the heading `## 0. Short version`. Then guards check the patterns that the three sentences of the Short version state:
- asmread of part L: its range does not overlap the 8000 MT/s pool and lies above it.
- asmread of F72d12: its range overlaps the pool.
- Old read kernel, parts A and C: each range overlaps its 8000 MT/s range.
- Old read kernel, part L: its range does not overlap the pool and lies below it.
- Old read kernel, control I and F72d12: each range overlaps the pool.
- `bw_new read`, session 1, both rounds: no interval lies inside or below the 8000 MT/s range. So all 3 intervals lie above it.

- `inside(k)` is true when the 7200 MT/s range of a comparison lies fully inside its 8000 MT/s range. A guard needs this for oldread of F72d12 and of control I.
- `c_ro`, `c_ra`: the groups `read after oldread` and `read after asmread`. A guard needs the same number of drops in both.
- `i_short = len(L)` remembers the current end of the line list. The three sentences quote numbers of section 4. So `short_version` (line 477) builds them after section 4, and `render` inserts them at this index (line 1467).
- `V['short_version']` is set to `None` here. `short_version` fills it later (line 559).
